Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-05 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Liam Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Mark Liu (CedarBridge CTO), Ana Delgado (Network Lead), Paul O'Neill (InfoSec), Sofia Park (Cloud Eng), Rajesh Menon (DevOps), Procurement rep

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy): quick scan: cedar bridge wants private deployment, worried about cross-region traffic, routing through transit gateway, and private endpoints. security wants KMS + audit logs. procurement asked about pricing cadence.

--- Transcript body ---
00:00 Liam Carter (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intros on our side, I'm Liam, AE for Redwood Inference, and Priya with me is our solutions engineer. How about we kick off with a brief overview of what you folks are trying to achieve?
00:12 Mark Liu (CedarBridge, CTO): Sure. Thanks, Liam. We're looking at moving our internal LLM workloads off an ad-hoc on-prem fleet to something that gives predictable latency and cost. Primary requirement is private connectivity — no public endpoints exposed for inference. We're running AWS primary in us-east-1 and GCP europe-west1 for DR and EU compliance.
00:28 Priya Shah (Redwood SE): Got it. When you say private connectivity, do you mean VPC peering, a transit gateway, PrivateLink, or some combination? Also curious about your current NAT/egress setup and firewall stack.
00:40 Ana Delgado (Network Lead): We're evaluating TGW because we have multiple VPCs — prod, dev, analytics — and we want a hub-and-spoke so we don't create N-squared peering. We're also using a third-party firewall in a central account and a centralized NAT gateway for internet egress.
00:56 Paul O'Neill (InfoSec): From security, the non-negotiables are: all traffic must be internal, logs forwarded to our SIEM, KMS integration for keys, and audit trails for model artifacts. We also need support for SAML SSO and RBAC at the model/API level.
01:10 Liam Carter (Redwood AE): That's helpful. On the Redwood side, Private deployments can sit inside a customer VPC or connect via peering/Transit Gateway depending on what you prefer. We support PrivateLink-style endpoints on AWS and Private Service Connect on GCP as well as peering options. There are tradeoffs — peering is simple but doesn't scale well for lots of VPCs; TGW or interconnects give central routing but introduce a single choke point and some additional egress charge considerations.
01:35 Rajesh Menon (DevOps): Egress cost is huge for us. If inference tokens or model syncs cross regions, that will balloon. We're trying to keep training/model sync in eu-west and inference serving in us-east for latency to our app.
01:49 Priya Shah (Redwood SE): For the POC, we usually recommend starting with dedicated deployment in a single region and using prefix-based routing + kv cache co-location to minimize cross-region token traffic. If you need multi-region we can do model replication and pin certain endpoints to regions to avoid hop penalties.
02:05 Ana Delgado (Network Lead): Walk us through what the route tables look like if we put Redwood into our transit hub. Who owns the route propagation and how do we handle overlapping CIDRs?
02:18 Priya Shah (Redwood SE): If you attach the Redwood subnets as a spoke, the TGW will propagate routes to each spoke. We'd suggest using a unique /20 or similar block for the Redwood subnets to avoid overlapping with your internal VPCs. If overlap exists we can NAT or use SNAT at the firewall, but that's messy. We'll include an example route table in the follow-up.
02:36 Mark Liu (CedarBridge, CTO): Any constraints around PrivateLink with our firewall in the middle? The firewall needs to inspect traffic to and from the inference nodes.
02:46 Liam Carter (Redwood AE): You can route through the firewall but keep an eye on throughput and connection tracking limits — inference can be bursty. For high throughput, we usually recommend sizing firewall autoscaling or using a packet-forwarding model. Also, PrivateLink will present as ENIs in your VPC so firewall inspection is straightforward if you place it in the path.
03:05 Paul O'Neill (InfoSec): About KMS — we use a customer-managed key in AWS. Can Redwood integrate so logs and any model artifacts stored remain encrypted under our CMK?
03:15 Priya Shah (Redwood SE): Yes, we support KMS integration and can use your CMK for any at-rest encryption in the private deployment. For hosted we have separate keys; for Private we can either use your KMS in the customer's account or integrate via cross-account roles. We'll outline the exact IAM trust and required policies in the security pack.
03:35 Sofia Park (Cloud Eng): Regarding regions: we can't run in china or Russia. For Europe we need to be in europe-west1 (GCP) or eu-west-1 (AWS). Any latency impacts we should expect if our app front-end sits in us-east and models are in europe-west?
03:50 Priya Shah (Redwood SE): RTT will be higher for eu <-> us. For chat-style workloads you can pin model inference to the region nearest your users, or set smart routing rules (we can route based on geo or latency SLO). For CedarBridge's case a multi-region setup with read-replicas of KV cache and model weights in both regions is doable but increases storage and sync costs.
04:10 Ana Delgado (Network Lead): Does Redwood require any BGP setup with our transit provider or is the peering via AWS/GCP control plane sufficient?
04:21 Priya Shah (Redwood SE): For typical setups we use native TGW attachments or peering via cloud control planes. If you have an on-prem colocation and want direct connect/Cloud Interconnect, we can work with BGP — some customers prefer direct private connectivity for predictable latency. We'll capture both options in the diagram.
04:36 Mark Liu (CedarBridge, CTO): Any limits on number of connections or concurrent requests per node that we should plan for? We're targeting 10k QPS in aggregate for the pilot.
04:48 Priya Shah (Redwood SE): QPS planning depends on model size and batching. For 10k QPS we usually propose dedicated pools with autoscaling and multi-node sharding. We'll propose a sizing estimate after we get real token-per-request numbers. For the POC, start smaller and we can run a load test.
05:05 Liam Carter (Redwood AE): Procurement question — Priya, can you outline if dedicated capacity requires a monthly commit and what happens if we need burst capacity?
05:15 Priya Shah (Redwood SE): Dedicated is reserved capacity, usually a monthly or annual commit depending on contract. We offer burst options that let you exceed committed throughput at a higher rate. For the POC we can enable burst windows to simulate peak traffic.
05:29 Procurement rep (customer): On SLAs, we need matrix for uptime and latency percentiles. Also compliance docs — can you send SOC2 Type II and ISO attestation?
05:39 Liam Carter (Redwood AE): Absolutely, we'll send the latest SOC2/ISO docs. For Private deployments some of the compliance controls are implemented in your VPC but we'll provide a mapping.
05:48 Paul O'Neill (InfoSec): One concern: audit logs — we need queryable logs for inference requests and model access. Does Redwood push logs to our CloudWatch/Stackdriver or forward to our SIEM?
06:00 Priya Shah (Redwood SE): We can forward logs via CloudWatch logs or Pub/Sub to Stackdriver, or push via our SIEM connector. For Private deployments we can also mount a fluentd/forwarder into your VPC that ships logs to your SIEM. We'll document retention and sample queries.
06:16 Mark Liu (CedarBridge, CTO): About model versioning and rollouts — if we pin a model version in eu and another in us-east, do you handle canary traffic split?
06:27 Priya Shah (Redwood SE): Yes, our rollout layer supports canary and A/B splits per route. You can define traffic percentages per route and fallback policies. That will interact with routing — make sure traffic for a given session hits the right region to preserve KV cache locality.
06:40 Ana Delgado (Network Lead): Any gotchas with egress charges if we replicate models across accounts?
06:48 Priya Shah (Redwood SE): Model sync across accounts/regions will incur egress. Best practice: keep model weights in the same region as the serving endpoints or use object storage replication with lifecycle policies. We'll include a cost example in the follow-up pricing sketch.
07:02 Rajesh Menon (DevOps): For TLS termination — do you terminate in our VPC or on your side? We prefer terminating in our VPC so keys never leave our control.
07:13 Priya Shah (Redwood SE): In Private deployments you can terminate TLS in your VPC. We also support mTLS between services inside the VPC for extra auth. We'll outline certificate expectations and any ACME or cert rotation hooks.
07:30 Mark Liu (CedarBridge, CTO): Is there any automation required on our side for node upgrades or can Redwood orchestrate upgrades within our VPC?
07:38 Priya Shah (Redwood SE): We can orchestrate within your VPC using cross-account roles and a small agent pattern. For air-gapped/on-prem options we provide a deployable package. For VPC-hosted Private, Redwood handles rolling upgrades with canary policies if you give the necessary IAM permissions.
07:55 Liam Carter (Redwood AE): Let's surface open risks: overlapping CIDRs, firewall throughput, cross-region egress cost, and KMS trust policies. Anything else?
08:06 Paul O'Neill (InfoSec): Data residency — ensure model training or any human-in-the-loop logs don't leave EU for EU-labeled requests.
08:14 Priya Shah (Redwood SE): That's enforceable via routing rules and region pinning — we can add request-level headers to route to the appropriate region and scrub logs accordingly.
08:26 Mark Liu (CedarBridge, CTO): Great. Can you include sample terraform snippets? Our infra team prefers terraform modules to attach TGW and set up endpoint services.
08:36 Priya Shah (Redwood SE): Yes, we have example terraform modules for TGW attachments, endpoint service creation, and route table propagation. We'll attach those to the follow-up.
08:45 Liam Carter (Redwood AE): Ok, recap of next steps: Priya will produce a transit topology diagram, sample route tables, and terraform snippets; I'll send pricing sketch and compliance pack; Mark to share account IDs and CIDRs. We'll reconvene for a POC kickoff the week of March 15. Any objections?
09:02 Mark Liu (CedarBridge, CTO): None from me. Thanks.
09:06 Ana Delgado (Network Lead): No objections. Please make sure the diagram shows where the firewall inspects traffic.
09:12 Paul O'Neill (InfoSec): And include the KMS integration flow and required IAM statements.
09:18 Liam Carter (Redwood AE): Will do. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
